title: Hidden Temporal Coupling in Tests
pattern: A test case that relies on a preceding test case running first to compute or initialize shared mutable state.
why_bad: It makes tests highly fragile and non-deterministic [450]. If the test runner executes tests in a parallel or randomized order, the tests will fail arbitrarily [421, 450].
detection: Test suites containing global mutable storage where one test writes state and another reads it without resetting in between.
counterexample: Explicit end-to-end integration scenario steps wrapped inside a single test method that runs strictly sequentially.
fix: Decouple the methods by passing parameters explicitly instead of relying on hidden global shared state [450]. Ensure every test is self-contained [421].
source:
*   *Clean Code*, "Hidden Temporal Coupling" (p. 258) [450]
*   *Refactoring*, "JUnit internals: Test isolation" (p. 421) [421]
